title: Xbash_Ransomware_Incident_Response_Scenario_ff3
description: Investigate the Xbash ransomware incident, identify indicators of compromise, and contain the threat.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content:
The victim host in your network has been compromised by the Xbash ransomware. This malware combines ransomware, coinmining, and worm-like self-propagation capabilities. It targets Linux-based systems for ransomware and botnet capabilities and Microsoft Windows-based systems for coinmining and self-propagation. The ransomware component targets and deletes Linux-based databases. It spreads by attacking weak passwords and unpatched vulnerabilities.

Your task is to investigate the incident, identify the indicators of compromise, and contain the threat.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have SSH access to the victim host with the following credentials:
- Hostname: victim
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano
Enter 'start' to begin.
levels.local_content:
To access the scenario, use the following credentials:
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano
Enter 'start' to begin.

levels.title: Identify the External Host
levels.content:
Identify the external host communicating with the compromised system.

Question: What is the IP address of the command-and-control server?

To discover the IP address, use the following command on the victim host:

`netstat -tuln`

This command will display active network connections. Look for connections to external IPs that are not part of your internal network. The IP address should be clearly visible in the output.
levels.solution: Check the network connections and logs on the victim host. The IP address of the command-and-control server is 192.168.90.5.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use the `netstat -tuln` command to check active network connections on the victim host. The IP address should be clearly visible in the output.

levels.title: Determine the Network Port
levels.content:
Determine which network port is used for suspicious command-and-control communication.

Question: What is the port number used for the command-and-control communication?

To discover the port number, use the following command on the victim host:

`netstat -tuln`

This command will display active network connections. Look for the port number associated with the external IP address identified in the previous task. The port number should be clearly visible in the output.
levels.solution: Investigate the network traffic and logs on the victim host. The port number used for the command-and-control communication is 4443.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use the `netstat -tuln` command to investigate network traffic and identify the port number associated with the external IP address. The port number should be clearly visible in the output.

levels.title: Identify Exfiltrated File
levels.content:
Identify a file or a dataset that was transferred outside the environment before encryption.

Question: What is the name of a file that was exfiltrated from the victim host?

To discover the exfiltrated file, use the following command on the victim host:

`grep -r 'quarterly_report.txt' /var/log/`

This command will search for references to the file in the system logs. The file name should be clearly visible in the output.
levels.solution: Analyze the logs and file access records on the victim host. The name of a file that was exfiltrated from the victim host is quarterly_report.txt.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use the `grep -r 'quarterly_report.txt' /var/log/` command to search for references to the file in the system logs. The file name should be clearly visible in the output.
